records.title: Three-step number chain
records.originality_disclosure: Newly authored problem scenario and wording. Not a reproduction of the observed SOF question stems, option sets or figures; global prior-art uniqueness is not established.
records.question_text: A student claims that multiplying any three consecutive positive integers always gives a multiple of 6. Prove or disprove the claim for every positive starting integer n, without checking only sample values.
records.expected_answer: The claim is true for every positive integer n.
records.worked_solution: Among n, n+1, and n+2, at least one is even, giving a factor of 2. Exactly one is divisible by 3, giving a factor of 3. Because 2 and 3 are coprime, their product n(n+1)(n+2) is divisible by 6.
records.independent_reverse_or_alternate_check: Write n=3k,3k+1,or 3k+2: one of the three factors is divisible by 3 in every case. Independently, parity alternates across adjacent integers, so at least one factor is even.
records.student_error_to_diagnose: Checking three examples cannot prove a universal claim.
records.protected_cognitive_decision: Show both factors 2 and 3 occur for all n; do not infer universal divisibility from numerical samples.

records.title: Compass notes to coordinates
records.originality_disclosure: Newly authored problem scenario and wording. Not a reproduction of the observed SOF question stems, option sets or figures; global prior-art uniqueness is not established.
records.question_text: On a map, east is the positive x-direction and north is the positive y-direction. A location is described as 4 kilometres west and 3 kilometres north of the origin. Express its location as an ordered pair (x,y), in kilometres.
records.worked_solution: Moving west decreases the x-coordinate by 4, so x=-4. Moving north increases the y-coordinate by 3, so y=+3. Write x before y to obtain (-4,3).
records.independent_reverse_or_alternate_check: Read the answer back: x=-4 means 4 kilometres west, and y=3 means 3 kilometres north; the verbal directions are recovered exactly.
records.student_error_to_diagnose: Reversing the order of x and y produces a different point.
records.protected_cognitive_decision: Preserve the sign conventions and the ordered (x,y) coordinate positions when translating compass directions.

records.title: Two movable triangle peaks
records.originality_disclosure: Newly authored problem scenario and wording. Not a reproduction of the observed SOF question stems, option sets or figures; global prior-art uniqueness is not established.
records.question_text: Triangles ABC and ABD share a 12 cm base AB. The perpendicular distance from C to line AB is 7 cm, and the perpendicular distance from D to that line is also 7 cm; C and D need not be directly above each other. Must the two triangles have the same area? Give the reason and their area.
records.expected_answer: Yes. Each area is 42 square centimetres.
records.worked_solution: A triangle's area is one-half times base length times perpendicular altitude. Both triangles have the same base length 12 cm and perpendicular altitude 7 cm. Each area is (1/2)*12*7=42 cm² regardless of the horizontal position of the third vertex.
records.independent_reverse_or_alternate_check: On the coordinate plane take A=(0,0),B=(12,0),C=(2,7),D=(10,7). Their determinant areas both equal |12*7|/2=42; shifting a peak parallel to the base preserves altitude.
records.student_error_to_diagnose: A slanted side is not the perpendicular altitude.
records.protected_cognitive_decision: Explain why equal base and perpendicular height, rather than identical side shapes, guarantee equal areas.

records.title: Ribbon around a cylindrical drum
records.originality_disclosure: Newly authored problem scenario and wording. Not a reproduction of the observed SOF question stems, option sets or figures; global prior-art uniqueness is not established.
records.question_text: A cylindrical festival drum has radius 7 cm and height 20 cm. A decorator covers only the curved side of the drum with one layer of sheet material, leaving both circular ends uncovered. Using pi=22/7, calculate the required sheet area in square centimetres.
records.worked_solution: Unroll the curved cylinder wall into a rectangle of width circumference 2*pi*r and height 20 cm. Its area is 2*pi*7*20 =280*pi square centimetres. Using pi=22/7 gives 880 cm².
records.independent_reverse_or_alternate_check: The rectangle has width 2*(22/7)*7=44 cm and height 20 cm, giving 44*20=880 cm². Neither of the two circular ends is included.
records.student_error_to_diagnose: Adding circular top and base areas would overestimate sheet needed.
records.protected_cognitive_decision: Select only curved cylinder surface, model its unrolled rectangle and exclude uncovered end circles.

records.title: A decreasing data table
records.originality_disclosure: Newly authored problem scenario and wording. Not a reproduction of the observed SOF question stems, option sets or figures; global prior-art uniqueness is not established.
records.question_text: A relation is recorded by four paired measurements: when x is -2, 0, 2, 4, the corresponding y-values are 9, 5, 1, -3. Express the pattern as an equation y=mx+c, then find x when y=-9.
records.worked_solution: When x rises by 2, y falls by 4, so slope m=-4/2=-2. At x=0, y=5, hence intercept c=5. Therefore y=-2x+5. Solving -9=-2x+5 gives -14=-2x and x=7.
records.independent_reverse_or_alternate_check: Verify two nonadjacent pairs: x=-2 gives 4+5=9 and x=4 gives -8+5=-3. Substitution x=7 gives y=-14+5=-9.
records.student_error_to_diagnose: Treating the change -4 in y as the slope ignores that x changed by 2.
records.protected_cognitive_decision: Preserve the row pairing, divide changes in y by changes in x, then use the resulting equation to invert the target.

records.title: Booklet and poster printing costs
records.originality_disclosure: Newly authored problem scenario and wording. Not a reproduction of the observed SOF question stems, option sets or figures; global prior-art uniqueness is not established.
records.question_text: At a student-run print shop, 4 bound booklets and 3 poster cards cost 159 rupees. A different order of 2 bound booklets and 5 poster cards costs 181 rupees. Each item has a fixed unit price. Find the price of an order containing 3 booklets and 2 poster cards.
records.worked_solution: Let b be the price of a booklet and c the price of a card. Then 4b+3c=159 and 2b+5c=181. Doubling the second yields 4b+10c=362, so subtract the first: 7c=203, giving c=29. Then 4b+87=159 yields b=18. The new order costs 3*18+2*29=112 rupees.
records.independent_reverse_or_alternate_check: Original orders recompute to 4*18+3*29=159 and 2*18+5*29=181. The target 3*18+2*29=112 is consistent with both independent constraints.
records.student_error_to_diagnose: A single order cannot identify two independent unit prices; both equations must be used.
records.protected_cognitive_decision: Choose two per-item variables, model both invoices jointly, eliminate one unknown, and check the forecast against both originals.

records.title: Reflect and move a triangle
records.originality_disclosure: Newly authored problem scenario and wording. Not a reproduction of the observed SOF question stems, option sets or figures; global prior-art uniqueness is not established.
records.question_text: Triangle PQR has vertices P=(-2,1), Q=(3,1), and R=(0,4). Reflect it across the y-axis, then translate every reflected point 4 units right and 2 units down. List the three final vertex coordinates and verify whether the triangle's area changes.
records.expected_answer: P''=(6,-1), Q''=(1,-1), R''=(4,2); area unchanged at 7.5 square units.
records.worked_solution: Reflection in the y-axis maps (x,y) to (-x,y). Translation maps (u,v) to (u+4,v-2). Thus P=(-2,1) becomes (2,1) then (6,-1); Q=(3,1) becomes (-3,1) then (1,-1); R=(0,4) becomes (0,4) then (4,2). The original horizontal base PQ is length 5 and altitude is 3, so area is 5*3/2=7.5. Reflection and translation preserve area.
records.independent_reverse_or_alternate_check: The determinant of (Q-P,R-P) is (5,0)x(2,3)=15; the final determinant of (Q''-P'',R''-P'') is (-5,0)x(-2,3)=-15. Absolute half-determinant is 7.5 in both cases.
records.student_error_to_diagnose: Reflection must be performed before translation; flipping y instead of x changes the image.
records.protected_cognitive_decision: Translate the ordered geometric operations into coordinates in sequence, then preserve the area invariant despite reversed orientation.
